usdRate.sourceName: European Central Bank euro reference rate (USD)
usdRate.note: EUR 1 = USD 1.1172, so about EUR 0.895 per US dollar; Croatia adopted the euro on 1 January 2023. World Bank 2025 average 0.885.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Trading Economics (Croatian Bureau of Statistics CPI, September 2026 final)
inflation_cpi.note: CPI 4.7% year on year in September 2026 (4.2% in August), final figure released 15 October 2026; secondary source because podaci.dzs.hr was not read directly. World Bank 2025 average 3.7%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: ECB 2% medium-term target; Croatian CPI 4.7% (Sep 2026), 3.7% in 2025 (World Bank)
inflation_projection.note: Croatia uses the euro and the ECB targets 2%, but Croatian inflation has run well above the euro-area average since euro adoption, so 3% is used for planning.

policy_rate.sourceName: European Central Bank, deposit facility rate
policy_rate.note: Croatia has used the euro since 2023; ECB deposit facility rate 2.50% (main refinancing rate 2.65%) from 16 September 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Croatian banks, household overnight deposits (new business)
savings_account_rate.note: Average 0.02% on household sight (a vista) deposits in September 2026 (also 0.02% in August), ECB MFI interest rate statistics.

fdr_3m_rate.note: ECB/HNB MFI statistics publish household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year as one bucket (1.55% in September 2026); hnb.hr was unreachable and no separate 3-month rate was found.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Croatian banks, household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year (new business)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Bucket covers all fixed terms up to one year; 1.55% in September 2026 (1.29% in August). Re-checked against the ECB data API by the verifier.

dps_rate.note: Croatia's regular-deposit savings product is housing savings (stambena štednja) at building societies with a state premium; no current average rate was found from an official source.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Croatian banks, household deposits with agreed maturity (outstanding amounts)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Average rate on all outstanding household term deposits, September 2026 (1.29% in August); World Bank FR.INR.DPST last reported 1.35% for 2014.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No 5-year retail government savings bond rate found; the Ministry of Finance sells 91-day treasury bills to citizens (2.75% in September 2026) and has issued occasional retail 'narodna obveznica' bonds, but no current issue or rate was read.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Ministry of Finance of Croatia, final terms of the 91-day treasury bill issue RHMF-T-651N
tbill_91d_rate.note: Competitive round annual yield 2.60%; the non-competitive retail round, taken up by about 37,000 investors, yielded 2.75%. Issued 17 September 2026.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No 5-year Croatian government bond yield found: Trading Economics shows only the 10-year yield and the Ministry of Finance bond pages read gave no secondary-market yields.

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: European Central Bank, long-term interest rate for convergence purposes (10-year government bond), Croatia
tbond_10y_rate.note: Official monthly average for September 2026 (3.58% in July and August). Trading Economics shows a market quote of 4.14% on 30 October 2026, which could not be reconciled with the official series, so the ECB figure is used.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Croatia income determination
tax_bank_interest.note: 12% final tax on interest; interest on current and sight accounts paying no more than 0.5% a year is exempt.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Croatia income determination
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: Interest on bonds and on debt securities of the Republic of Croatia, including treasury bills, is excluded from taxable interest income.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Croatian Deposit Insurance Agency (HAOD), secured amount
deposit_insurance_limit.note: EUR 100,000 per depositor per credit institution, including accrued interest.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: Croatian consumer credit law sets a maximum contractual interest rate published by the HNB, but hnb.hr was unreachable and no current figure or typical card rate was found.

equity_return_low.sourceName: CROBEX 4,471 on 30 Oct 2026, up 17% in a year but still below its 2007 peak of 5,393
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Croatian shares earn little more than tax-free treasury bills over long periods, as in the 19 years since the 2007 peak.

equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 3.4 points over the tax-free treasury bill rate, kept modest because the CROBEX is small, illiquid and has not regained its 2007 high.

equity_return_high.sourceName: CROBEX (Trading Economics); global equity long-run returns
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified euro equity fund matching long-run global equity returns of about 8% in euros.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD 3,876/oz on 30 Oct 2026, 31% below the January 2026 high
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps up after the 2025-26 spike, with no help from the euro.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); ECB 2% inflation target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises roughly with world inflation plus a little, and the euro is assumed stable against the dollar over the long run.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in euro terms.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 1.55% (September 2026) less 12% tax = 1.36% (ECB MFI statistics)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: bank term deposits after the 12% interest tax, allowing for deposit rates to slip back.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Ministry of Finance 91-day treasury bills 2.60-2.75%, tax-free
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: rolling tax-free retail treasury bills, slightly below the September 2026 yield as ECB rates may ease.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Croatia 10-year government bond 3.59% (ECB, September 2026), interest tax-free
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: holding longer Croatian government bonds, whose interest is untaxed, just below the current 10-year yield.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: HANFA and the Croatian Insurance Bureau publish premium and claims totals but no industry life claim settlement ratio could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life (rizično životno osiguranje) is sold, but no published premium table or regulator data on term premiums per sum insured was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital care is covered by HZZO compulsory insurance, with co-payments covered by supplementary insurance (dopunsko osiguranje); no official figure for a typical out-of-pocket private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Supplementary and private health insurance are sold at flat premiums, not per sum insured, and no premium table per EUR 100,000 of cover was found.

oop_health_share.note: Latest World Bank/WHO figure is for 2023 (older than 2025); no newer official figure was found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Eurostat/ECB HICP Croatia, health: 4.3% year on year in December 2025
goal_inflation_health.note: Health prices rise about as fast as Croatia's above-target headline inflation; 4.5% is used for planning.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Eurostat/ECB HICP Croatia, education: -1.0% year on year in December 2025
goal_inflation_education.note: The education index fell in 2025 because public schooling and textbooks are free, so private education costs are assumed to rise a little above general inflation at 3.5%.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 76.0, women 82.1 (UN WPP estimate for 2026, mid-year); World Bank 2024 figure 78.9.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 37.7 (2025, World Bank), 47.1 (2040) and 58.4 (2065, populationpyramid.net/croatia/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Croatian Pension Insurance Institute (HZMO), old-age pension
retirement_age_default.note: 65 with at least 15 years of insurance for anyone born after 1975, men and women; women retiring in 2026 can go at 64 years 0 months, rising to 65 from 1 January 2030. The Labour Act also ends employment at 65 with 15 years of pension service unless agreed otherwise.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Civil Servants Act (Zakon o državnim službenicima, NN 155/23, 85/24), Article 152
retirement_age_government.note: Article 152: civil service ends at 65 with at least 15 years of pension service, extendable by agreement up to 67; consolidated text current to NN 119/26 (re-checked on zakon.hr).

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 1.55% (September 2026) less 12% tax = 1.36% (ECB MFI statistics)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: bank term deposits after tax, allowing for deposit rates to slip back.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Ministry of Finance 91-day treasury bills 2.60-2.75%, tax-free
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped just below the tax-free retail treasury bill yield.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Croatia 10-year government bond 3.59% (ECB, September 2026), interest tax-free
retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of tax-free Croatian government bonds, below the current 10-year yield.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 6% and half tax-free government paper at about 2.5-3.5%.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: HZMO, national benefit for older persons (nacionalna naknada za starije osobe)
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: EUR 160.22 a month from 1 January 2026 for people aged 65+ with no pension.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: HZMO, national benefit for older persons
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Croatian citizens aged 65+ with 10 years' continuous residence, no pension, and household income per member below EUR 320.44 a month (twice the benefit).

gratuity_rule.note: Severance (otpremnina) only on dismissal by the employer after 2 years' continuous service: at least one third of average monthly pay per year of service (about 10 days), capped at 6 months' pay; not paid on retirement at 65 with 15 years of pension service.

public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory pay-as-you-go first pillar plus a mandatory second-pillar fund; pensions are adjusted on 1 January and 1 July by a mix of consumer-price inflation and average gross wage growth. Women's pension age reaches 65 in 2030.

dps.note: Regular saving with building societies, with a state incentive on yearly deposits.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No standing 5-year savings bond for individuals; the government issues occasional retail bonds and sells 91-day treasury bills to citizens, with interest tax-free.

tbill_91d.localNameEn: Treasury bills of the Ministry of Finance
tbill_91d.note: Citizens can subscribe in a non-competitive retail round.

equity_fund.note: Gains on financial assets held over two years are not taxed.

gold.note: No restriction on buying physical gold.

centralBank.name: Hrvatska narodna banka (Croatian National Bank)
centralBank.note: Part of the Eurosystem since 2023; monetary policy set by the European Central Bank.

insuranceRegulator.name: Hrvatska agencija za nadzor financijskih usluga (HANFA)

oldAgeAllowance.name: Nacionalna naknada za starije osobe (national benefit for older persons)

statistics.name: Državni zavod za statistiku (Croatian Bureau of Statistics)
